readings.subsection: Asa's Reliance on the Adversary's System
readings.title: The Treacherous Bribe of Ben-Hadad
readings.subtitle: Asa funds a proxy war using the Covenant's treasuries, breaking trust with YeHoVaH.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 15:16] And there was fighting between Asa and Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl all their days.
[17] And Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl came up against Yehuḏah, and built <dn>את</dn> Ramah, to keep anyone from going out or coming in to Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah.
[18] And Asa took <dn>את</dn> all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the treasuries of the sovereign’s house, and gave them into the hand of his servants. And Sovereign Asa sent them to Ben-Haḏaḏ son of Taḇrimmon, son of Ḥezyon, sovereign of Aram, who dwelt in Dammeseq, saying,
[19] “Let there be a covenant between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. Look, <dn>I</dn> have sent you a present of silver and gold. Come, break your covenant with Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl, so that he withdraws from me.”
[20] And Ben-Haḏaḏ listened to Sovereign Asa, and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Yisra’ěl, and struck Iyon, and Dan, and Aḇěl Běyth Ma‛aḵah, and all Kinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.
[21] And it came to be, when Ba‛asha heard it, that he stopped building Ramah, and remained in Tirtsah.
[22] Then Sovereign Asa summoned all Yehuḏah – none was exempted – and they took away <dn>את</dn> the stones and timber of Ramah, which Ba‛asha had used for building. And with them Sovereign Asa built Geḇa of Binyamin, and Mitspah.

readings.title: Stripping the Treasuries
readings.subtitle: Asa architects an alliance with Aram to neutralize the physical threat of Baasha, ignoring the divine hedge of protection.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 16:1] In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Ba‛asha the sovereign of Yisra’ěl came up against Yehuḏah and built <dn>את</dn> Ramah, to prevent anyone going out or coming in to Asa, sovereign of Yehuḏah.
[2] And Asa brought silver and gold from the treasuries of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and of the sovereign’s house, and sent to Ben-Haḏaḏ sovereign of Aram, who dwelt in Darmeseq, saying,
[3] “Let there be a covenant between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. See, <dn>I</dn> have sent you silver and gold. Come, break your covenant with Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl, so that he withdraws from me.”
[4] And Ben-Haḏaḏ listened to Sovereign Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Yisra’ěl, and they struck Iyon, and Dan, and Aḇěl Mayim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.
[5] And it came to be, when Ba‛asha heard it, that he stopped building Ramah and ceased his work.
[6] Then Asa the sovereign brought all Yehuḏah, and they took away <dn>את</dn> the stones and timber of Ramah, which Ba‛asha had used for building. And with them he built Geḇa and Mitspah.

readings.title: The Failure of Emunah
readings.subtitle: Hanani exposes Asa's broken trust, revealing that reliance on earthly powers shatters systemic harmony and guarantees perpetual conflict.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 16:7] And at that time Ḥanani the seer came to Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, and said to him, “Because you have relied on the sovereign of Aram, and have not relied on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, therefore the army of the sovereign of Aram has escaped from your hand.
[8] “Were the Kushites and the Luḇim not a mighty army with very many chariots and horsemen? And because you relied on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> gave them into your hand.
[9] “For the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> diligently search throughout all the earth, to show <dn>Himself</dn> to be strong on behalf of those whose heart is perfect to <dn>Him</dn>. You have acted foolishly in this, so from now on you shall have battles.”
[10] And Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in prison, for he was enraged at him because of this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.

readings.title: The Prophetic Decree of Ruin
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's word sweeps against Baasha for cultivating the systemic disharmony (Ra) of Jeroboam.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 16:1] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yěhu son of Ḥanani, against Ba‛asha, saying,
[2] <dq>“Because <dn>I</dn> raised you up out of the dust and made you ruler over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl, but you walked in the way of Yaroḇ‛am, and made <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl sin, to provoke <dn>Me</dn> with their sins,</dq>
[3] <dq>see, <dn>I</dn> am going to sweep away Ba‛asha and his house, and shall make your house like the house of Yaroḇ‛am the son of Neḇat.</dq>
[4] <dq>“Anyone belonging to Ba‛asha who dies in a city the dogs eat, and anyone belonging to him who dies in a field the birds of the heavens eat.”</dq>
[5] And the rest of the acts of Ba‛asha, what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl?
[6] So Ba‛asha slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirtsah. And his son Ělah reigned in his place.
[7] Moreover, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came by the prophet Yěhu son of Ḥanani against Ba‛asha and his house, because of all the evil that he did in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in provoking <dn>Him</dn> with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Yaroḇ‛am, and because he struck <dn>את</dn> them.

readings.title: Zimri's Calculated Assassination
readings.subtitle: Zimri executes the prophesied destruction upon Elah, wiping out the entire household in an act of violent usurpation.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 16:8] In the twenty-sixth year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, Ělah son of Ba‛asha began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Tirtsah, two years.
[9] And his servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, conspired against him as he was in Tirtsah drinking himself drunk in the house of Artsa, who was over his house in Tirtsah.
[10] Then Zimri came in and struck him and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, and reigned in his place.
[11] And it came to be, when he began to reign, as soon as he was seated on his throne, that he struck <dn>את</dn> all the household of Ba‛asha. He did not leave him one male, neither of his relatives nor of his friends.
[12] So Zimri destroyed the entire house of Ba‛asha, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> spoke against Ba‛asha by Yěhu the prophet,
[13] for all the sins of Ba‛asha and the sins of Ělah his son, by which they had sinned and by which they had made Yisra’ěl sin, in provoking <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl with their worthlessnesses.
[14] And the rest of the acts of Ělah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl?

readings.title: The Seven-Day Reign of Zimri
readings.subtitle: Facing the unified strength of Omri's forces, Zimri ends his own life, consumed by the consequences of his lawlessness.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 16:15] In the twenty-seventh year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirtsah. And the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
[16] And the people who were encamped heard it said, “Zimri has conspired and also struck <dn>את</dn> the sovereign.” So all Yisra’ěl set up Omri, the commander of the army, to reign over Yisra’ěl that day in the camp.
[17] And Omri went up, and all Yisra’ěl with him, from Gibbethon, and they besieged Tirtsah.
[18] And it came to be, when Zimri saw that the city was captured, that he went into a high place of the sovereign’s house and burned <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s house down upon himself with fire, and died,
[19] because of the sins which he had sinned in doing evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in walking in the way of Yaroḇ‛am, and in his sin which he had committed to make Yisra’ěl sin.
[20] And the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the conspiracy he made, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl?

readings.title: Purchasing the Hill of Shomeron
readings.subtitle: Omri consolidates absolute power, establishing a new geopolitical epicenter and plunging Israel deeper into systemic rebellion.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 16:21] Then the people of Yisra’ěl were divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tiḇni son of Ginath, to make him reign, and half followed Omri.
[22] But the people who followed Omri were stronger than the people who followed Tiḇni son of Ginath. And Tiḇni died and Omri reigned.
[23] In the thirty-first year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, Omri became sovereign over Yisra’ěl, and reigned twelve years. He reigned six years in Tirtsah.
[24] And he bought <dn>את</dn> the hill of Shomeron from Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called <dn>את</dn> the name of the city which he built, Shomeron, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill.
[25] And Omri did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and did evil more than all those before him,
[26] and walked in all the ways of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, and in his sin by which he had made Yisra’ěl sin, provoking <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl with their worthlessnesses.
[27] And the rest of the acts of Omri which he did, and the might that he attained, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl?
[28] So Omri slept with his fathers and was buried in Shomeron. And Aḥaḇ his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: Ahab's Alliance with Jezebel
readings.subtitle: Ahab merges state authority with Baal worship, brazenly violating the Covenant more than any predecessor.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 16:29] In the thirty-eighth year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, Aḥaḇ son of Omri became sovereign over Yisra’ěl. And Aḥaḇ son of Omri reigned over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron twenty-two years.
[30] And Aḥaḇ son of Omri did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, more than all those before him.
[31] And it came to be, as though it had been a light matter for him to walk in the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, that he took as wife <dn>את</dn> Izeḇel the daughter of Ethba‛al, sovereign of the Tsiḏonians. And he went and served Ba‛al and bowed himself to it,
[32] and raised up a slaughter-place for Ba‛al in the house of Ba‛al, which he had built in Shomeron.
[33] And Aḥaḇ made <dn>את</dn> an Ashěrah. And Aḥaḇ did more to provoke <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl than all the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl before him.

readings.title: Rebuilding Jericho
readings.subtitle: Hiel ignores the ancient oath, paying the horrific ultimate price of his sons to re-establish the forbidden city.
readings.text: [1 Kings 16:34] In his days Ḥi’ěl of Běyth Ěl built <dn>את</dn> Yeriḥo. He laid its foundation at the cost of Aḇiram his first-born, and at the cost of his youngest son Seḡuḇ he set up its gates, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> had spoken through Yehoshua son of Nun.

readings.title: The Diseased Feet of a King
readings.subtitle: The chronicles record Asa's acts, culminating in severe physical affliction in his final days.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 15:23] And the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
[24] So Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ his father. And Yehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: Trusting Physicians over the Creator
readings.subtitle: In his terminal state, Asa refuses to seek YeHoVaH's restorative justice, placing his absolute trust in human medicine.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 16:11] And look, the acts of Asa, the first and the last, see, they are written in the book of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah and Yisra’ěl.
[12] And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his disease was severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but the physicians.
[13] So Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign.
[14] And they buried him in his burial-site, which he had made for himself in the City of Daviḏ. And they laid him in the bed which was filled with spices and various kinds of ointments mixed by the perfumer’s skill. And they made a very great burning for him.

readings.title: Walking in the Former Ways
readings.subtitle: Yehoshaphat anchors his governance in Emunah, eradicating pagan structures and securing divine establishment.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 17:1] And Yehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and strengthened himself against Yisra’ěl,
[2] and placed an army in all the walled cities of Yehuḏah, and set watch-posts in the land of Yehuḏah and in the cities of Ephrayim which Asa his father had taken.
[3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with Yehoshaphat, for he walked in the former ways of his father Daviḏ, and did not seek the Ba‛als,
[4] but sought the <dn>Elohim</dn> of his father, and walked in <dn>His</dn> commands and not according to the deeds of Yisra’ěl.
[5] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> established the reign in his hand. And all Yehuḏah gave presents to Yehoshaphat, and he had great riches and esteem.
[6] And his heart was exalted in the ways of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he again removed <dn>את</dn> the high places and <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrim from Yehuḏah.

readings.title: Deploying the Torah
readings.subtitle: Officials and Levites are commissioned to circulate the Book of the Torah, structurally repairing the nation's spiritual intelligence.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 17:7] And in the third year of his reign he sent his leaders, Ben-Ḥayil, and Oḇaḏyah, and Zeḵaryah, and Nethan’ěl, and Miḵayahu, to teach in the cities of Yehuḏah.
[8] And with them he sent Lěvites: Shemayahu, and Nethanyahu, and Zeḇaḏyahu, and Asah’ěl, and Shemiramoth, and Yehonathan, and Aḏoniyahu, and Toḇiyahu, and Toḇaḏoniyah, the Lěvites, and with them Elishama and Yehoram, the priests.
[9] And they taught in Yehuḏah, and with them was the Book of the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they went around into all the cities of Yehuḏah and taught the people.

readings.title: The Wealth of Systemic Harmony
readings.subtitle: Neighboring nations submit via the fear of YeHoVaH, generating a massive influx of economic surplus for Judah.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 17:10] And the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fell on all the reigns of the lands that were around Yehuḏah, and they did not fight against Yehoshaphat.
[11] And some of the Philistines brought Yehoshaphat gifts and a load of silver. And the Araḇians brought him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
[12] And Yehoshaphat became increasingly great, and he built palaces and storage cities in Yehuḏah.
[13] And he had much work in the cities of Yehuḏah. And the men of battle, mighty brave men, were in Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Mighty Brave Men
readings.subtitle: A meticulously organized, high-capacity standing army is established under Yehoshaphat's command.

readings.title: The Decree of Drought at Kerith
readings.subtitle: Elijah executes divine authority to halt the physical rain, establishing YeHoVaH's absolute supremacy over Ahab's agricultural economy.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 17:1] And Ěliyahu the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gil‛aḏ, said to Aḥaḇ, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl lives, before whom <dn>I</dn> stand, there shall be no dew or rain these years, except at my word.”
[2] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to him, saying,
[3] <dq>“Go away from here and turn eastward, and hide by the wadi Kerith, which flows into the Yarděn.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And it shall be that you drink from the stream, and <dn>I</dn> shall command <dn>את</dn> the ravens to feed you there.”</dq>
[5] And he went and did according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for he went and dwelt by the wadi Kerith, which flows into the Yarděn.
[6] And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the stream.
[7] And it came to be after a while that the stream dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
